item.title: Roscommon woman who died in crash made a 'massive contribution to society', funeral hears
item.description: The funeral Mass of a Roscommon woman who died in a Galway crash has heard she made a 'massive contribution to society'. Kathleen Cunningham has also been remembered as a woman of 'deep faith', who spent the final day of her life at Knock Shrine. The 80-year-old, who lived in Toomard, Newbridge, Co Galway, was originally from Tibohine, outside Ballaghaderreen. item.title: Over 500 local drivers slapped with penalty points for mobile-phone offence
item.description: Over 500 people in the Shannonside region were given penalty points for holding a mobile phone while driving last year. More than 3,000 drivers got points for speeding, according to figures from the Department of Transport. You can legally talk on your phone while driving using a hands-free kit, but not while holding the handset. Advertisement For doing so, you face an automatic fine of €120 and three penalty points. item.title: Planned eating-disorder unit in Roscommon 'long overdue' - councillor
item.description: The planned eating disorder unit for Roscommon is being described as a 'massively positive development'. The six-bed ward will be part of the new mental health unit in Roscommon, which is planned by the HSE. This will replace the outdated department of psychiatry in Roscommon University Hospital. item.title: Fresh hopes Boyle will get state childcare centre
item.description: There are hopes Boyle will be one of the locations to receive a new state-led childcare facility. Children's Minister Norma Foley says her department will buy properties to house state-led childcare facilities this year, but the building of such will start in 2027. A meeting in Boyle last year heard 77 per cent of children aged under four are currently unable to access childcare services. item.title: 170 jobs created by LEO-backed businesses in Roscommon in 2025
item.description: Businesses backed by the Local Enterprise Office created over 170 new jobs in Roscommon last year. That's according to senior executive development officer Enda Cannon, who was speaking ahead of Local Enterprise Week. The annual initiative runs from Monday to Friday next and will see events taking place across the Shannonside region. item.title: Motor insurance price has dropped by a third in a decade - local minister
item.description: A local minister says the cost of motor insurance is a third cheaper now compared to 10 years ago. Junior Finance Minister Robert Troy was speaking as Government continue with their action plan to reduce insurance costs. It was launched last year and will run until 2029. item.title: Local man who was former Irish ambassador to Brazil, passes away
item.description: A former Irish ambassador to Brazil has passed away. Frank Sheridan, who's originally from Athlone, died peacefully in the Beacon Hospital last weekend. His funeral mass is taking place tomorrow morning at 11am in St. Fergal’s Church, Boghall Road, Bray. Advertisement

item.title: Number of people in the region who were banned from driving last year increases
item.description: The number of people in the Shannonside region who were banned from driving increased by over a fifth last year. They were either disqualified by the courts or because they got too many penalty points. There are two ways a driver can get disqualified from driving. A judge can ban them in court, or you can get disqualified because you get too many penalty points - 12 for a fully qualified driver or seven for a learner or novice motorist. item.title: Local TD criticises Government's handling of ongoing Bord Bia dispute
item.description: The government has come under fire for the oversight and future direction of Bord Bia. Sligo-Leitrim TD Martin Kenny raised concerns about transparency, expenditure, and accountability within the semi-state agency. The calls come as a special board meeting of Bord Bia will take place next Monday to discuss the ongoing dispute with farmers. item.title: PFAI vote against Ireland playing Isreal
item.description: The Professional footballers of Ireland have voted against Ireland facing Israel in the nation’s league. The Professional football association of Ireland (PFAI) members voted 63% against Ireland fulfilling the fixture. Whereas, two-thirds of members saying they will not attend the game if goes ahead. 66% of members voted against attending the game, 79% of those members say that was due to moral reasons.
